The '''2007–08 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 106th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 76th in a [[round-robin tournament]]. It started on 25 August 2007 and ended on 18 May 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Primo_Piano/2007/06_Giugno/21/campionato26.shtml| author=Gazzetta dello Sport| author-link=Gazzetta dello Sport|title=Abete, ok "con rammarico". La serie A parte il 26 agosto|date=2007-06-21|access-date=2007-06-22|language=it}}</ref> [[F.C. Internazionale Milano|Internazionale Milano]] successfully defended the championship on the final day of the season, finishing first with 85 points, three ahead of [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].

==Events==

===''Plusvalenze'' investigation===
Inquiries are being conducted by the ''CO.VI.SOC.'' (Italian football's financial watchdogs) into the finances of four Serie A clubs ([[Inter Milan|Internazionale]], [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], and [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]]) who stand accused of falsely inflating player values — a practice known as ''plusvalenze'' in Italian — in order to qualify financially for the [[2005–06 Serie A]]. If the allegations prove true, penalties could range from fines to point deductions, relegation to Serie B, and even the stripping of Internazionale's 2005-06 ''[[scudetto]]'', which was stripped from [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] as a result of the ''[[Calciopoli]]'' scandal before being awarded to Internazionale.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun20x.html |author=Football Italia |author-link=Football Italia |title=Could Inter be demoted? |date=2007-06-20 |access-date=2007-06-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070626112715/http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun20x.html |archive-date=2007-06-26 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Lazio fan killed by police===
{{main|Murder of Gabriele Sandri}}
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:Gabriele Sandri Stadio Olimpico.JPG|left|thumb|200px|Banner depicting Gabriele Sandri, displayed by Lazio supporters in the [[Curva (stadia)|Curva]] Nord of the [[Stadio Olimpico]] in [[Rome]].]] -->
On the morning of 11 November 2007 26-year-old [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] fan [[Gabriele Sandri]], a [[DJ]] from Rome, was killed by a shot in his neck while sitting inside a car,<ref>{{cite news| url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7090170.stm | work=BBC News | title=Officer 'rues' killing Lazio fan | date=2007-11-12 | access-date=2010-04-22}}</ref> by a policeman, after some other fans of Lazio violently assaulted a group of [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] ultras with stones on the [[A1 Motorway (Italy)|A1 Motorway]] service station of Badia al Pino in [[Arezzo]].<ref name="fandeath">{{cite news|url=http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/nov11g.html |author=Football Italia |author-link=Football Italia |title=Lazio fan killed - Serie A stopped? |date=2007-11-11 |access-date=2007-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071113010039/http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/nov11g.html |archive-date=2007-11-13 |url-status=live }}</ref> Early reports suggested that a [[bullet|stray bullet]] from a gun, set to distract the group of [[ultras]], hit the Lazio fan in the neck as he sat in a car and killed him.<ref name="fandeath" /> An emergency meeting set up between [[Lega Nazionale Professionisti|Lega Calcio]] president [[Antonio Matarrese]] and police chief Antonio Manganelli decided that the game between [[F.C. Internazionale Milano|Inter]] and Lazio would be called off, but the rest of the fixtures would go ahead that day, starting at a slightly later time (about 10 minutes later).<ref name="sandrilazio">{{cite news|url=http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/nov11i.html |author=Football Italia |author-link=Football Italia |title=Inter-Lazio Off |date=2007-11-11 |access-date=2007-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071112235250/http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/nov11i.html |archive-date=2007-11-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> The Atalanta–Milan game was eventually suspended following unrest caused by local ultras attempting to break off the protection glass in order to invade the pitch and stop the match. Later in the afternoon, the Italian Football Federation chose to postpone also the game between AS Roma and Cagliari, whose kick off was scheduled for 8:30 pm at [[Stadio Olimpico]], Rome. However, this did not prevent violent riots, as hundreds of armed hooligans attacked a police barracks and the CONI (Italian Olympic National Committee) headquarters in Rome.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7090017.stm|work=BBC News|date=2007-11-12|access-date=2007-11-15|title=Italy fans rampage after killing| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20071113103923/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7090017.stm| archive-date= 13 November 2007 | url-status= live}}</ref>

Though Sandri's death was later held by some to have been caused by a tragic error by a policeman who claimed his gun went off as he was running.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7090170.stm|access-date=2007-11-15|date=2007-11-12|title=Officer 'rues' killing Lazio fan|work=BBC News| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20071114112237/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7090170.stm| archive-date= 14 November 2007 | url-status= live}}</ref> Prosecutors then opted initially to open an inquiry into manslaughter against the policeman,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7091849.stm|access-date=2007-11-15|date=2007-11-12|title=Probe starts on Italy fan death|work=BBC News| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20071115101959/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7091849.stm| archive-date= 15 November 2007 | url-status= live}}</ref> nevertheless the initial hearing held that Sandri's death was culpable homicide, and the policeman involved (Luigi Spaccarotella) was condemned to 6 years imprisonment. On appeal, the higher court not only confirmed this judgment, but increased the punishment to 9 years and 4 months as an element of intentionality was found.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/cronaca/2010/12/01/news/sandri_appello-9743836/|access-date=2010-12-04|date=2007-11-12|title=Sandri- fu omicidio volontario|publisher=La Repubblica in Italian}}</ref>

===Final week===
The championship was decided in the final week, as [[Inter Milan|Inter]], who managed to secure even an 11-point advantage to rivals [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] in mid-season, lost almost all of it in the final weeks, maintaining only a one-point advantage with only one match to play. In the final week, both Inter and Roma were scheduled to play away matches opposed to relegation-battling sides, respectively [[Parma F.C.|Parma]] and [[Calcio Catania|Catania]]. Both matches were successively forbidden to be attended by Inter and Roma fans. In the end, Inter secured the ''scudetto'' with a 2–0 win, with both goals being scored in the second half by [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]], who recovered from a long-term injury in time to play the game, whereas Roma only managed to achieve a 1–1 draw at [[Stadio Angelo Massimino]] against [[Walter Zenga]]'s Catania, a result which allowed the Sicilian side to escape relegation at the expense of [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] and Parma.

===2007–08 events===
*'''Atalanta''': on June 9, 2007 [[Luigi Delneri]] was announced as new head coach following [[Stefano Colantuono]]'s departure to Palermo.<ref name="delneri_atalanta"/>
*'''Cagliari''': on November 13 Cagliari chairman [[Massimo Cellino]] sacked [[Marco Giampaolo]] and replaced him with veteran coach [[Nedo Sonetti]], who already served twice with the ''rossoblu'' before this new appointment.<ref name="giampaolo_sacked" /><ref name="sonetti_cagliari" /> On December 19 Sonetti tendered his resignation, after he managed to achieve only one point in three matches in charge, and Cellino called Giampaolo to serve again as ''rossoblu'' head coach.<ref name="sonetti_resignation">{{cite news |title=Sonetti si è dimesso |url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=4824&type=0&id_menu=1 |publisher=Cagliari Calcio |date=2007-12-19 |access-date=2007-12-19 |language=it |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071229055350/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=4824&type=0&id_menu=1 |archive-date=29 December 2007 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> However, Giampaolo, still linked to Cagliari by a contract, turned down the opportunity to return.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/dec19j.html |publisher=Football Italia |access-date=2007-12-19 |date=2007-12-19 |title=Giampaolo rejects Cagliari call |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071221155647/http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/dec19j.html |archive-date=2007-12-21 |url-status=live }}</ref> The next day, the club announced that it had rejected Sonetti's resignation.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=4828&type=0&id_menu=1 |publisher=Cagliari Calcio |language=it |title=Respinte le dimissioni di Sonetti |date=2007-12-20 |access-date=2007-12-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080412054956/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=4828&type=0&id_menu=1 |archive-date=2008-04-12 }}</ref> Sonetti was ultimately sacked only a few days later, on December 27, following a crushing 5–1 loss to Fiorentina, and replaced by [[Davide Ballardini]], who served as Cagliari head coach in the early weeks of the [[2005–06 Serie A|2005–06 season]].<ref name="sonetti_sacked" />
*'''Catania''': on June 3, 2007 [[Silvio Baldini]] was announced as new head coach.<ref name="baldini_catania"/> The team initially enjoyed a good shape, notably gaining a spot in the [[Coppa Italia]] semi-finals, but lost position with time, being in 16th place as of Week 31, only three points ahead of last-placed Empoli, convincing Baldini to leave the club with mutual consent on March 31, 2008.<ref name="baldini_resignation" /> He was replaced the next day by [[Walter Zenga]], former head coach of [[Red Star Belgrade]] and [[FC Steaua București|Steaua București]], at his first coaching experience with a Serie A team.<ref name="zenga_catania" />
*'''Empoli''': on November 26, 2007 the Tuscan side chose to sack [[Luigi Cagni]], who achieved only ten points in fourteen matches (18th place in the league table) and failed to win the [[2007–08 UEFA Cup]] first round, replacing him with [[Alberto Malesani]].<ref name="cagni_sacked" /> On March 31, 2008, after a 2–0 home loss to [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] which left Empoli alone in last place, the board decided to sack Malesani, reinstalling Cagni in charge.<ref name="malesani_sacked" />
*'''Juventus''': on June 4, 2007 former [[Parma F.C.|Parma]] head coach [[Claudio Ranieri]] was unveiled as new boss.<ref name="ranieri_juve"/>
*'''Livorno''': on October 9, 2007 [[Fernando Orsi]] was sacked following a string of poor results that brought the team down to bottom place in the league with two points and no win after seven games.<ref name="orsi_sacked" /> The position was then filled by [[Giancarlo Camolese]] the next day.<ref name="camolese_livorno" /> Camolese initially managed to improve Livorno's performances; however in the final part of the season Livorno entered into a deep result crisis that led them down to the league bottom, with three matches remaining, and Camolese being ultimately sacked on April 28, 2008, with Orsi re-appointed back at the helm of the ''amaranto''.<ref name="camolese_sacked" />
*'''Palermo''': on June 7, 2007 [[Stefano Colantuono]] of [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] was announced to be the next ''rosanero'' boss for the 2007-08 season.<ref name="colantuono_palermo"/> However, on November 26 Colantuono was sacked following a 5–0 defeat to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], and club chairman [[Maurizio Zamparini]] appointed [[Francesco Guidolin]] as his replacement, inaugurating a fourth spell with Palermo for the tactician.<ref name="colantuono_sacked" /> However, results did not improve under Guidolin, and three consecutive losses, followed by some controversial post-match comments in a 2–3 home loss to [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]] on March 22, 2008 led Zamparini to re-appoint Colantuono at the helm of the ''rosanero'' on March 24.<ref name="guidolin_sacked" />
*'''Parma''': on June 12, 2007 [[Domenico Di Carlo]] was announced as new boss following the departure of [[Claudio Ranieri]].<ref name="dicarlo_parma"/> However, as Parma struggled to keep themselves off the relegation battle, Di Carlo was sacked on March 10, 2008 following a 1–2 home defeat to [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]].<ref name="dicarlo_sacked" /> The next day the club announced to have appointed [[Héctor Cúper]] as new head coach.<ref name="cuper_parma" /> The [[Argentina|Argentine]] boss did not manage to improve results, with Parma finding themselves in 18th place with only one remaining match to be played at home against first-placed Internazionale, only two points behind the last Serie A spot. On May 12 Parma chairman [[Tommaso Ghirardi]] then surprisingly announced to have sacked Cúper, replacing him with youth team coach [[Andrea Manzo]] for the final league matchday in a desperate attempt to escape relegation.<ref name="cuper_sacked" />
*'''Reggina''': on June 23, 2007 news reports announced [[Massimo Ficcadenti]] as new boss following the departure of [[Walter Mazzarri]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun23n.html |publisher=Football Italia |title=Reggina appoint Ficcadenti |access-date=2007-06-24 |date=2007-06-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070712131738/http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun23n.html |archive-date=2007-07-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, on June 27 Verona announced they were not giving Ficcadenti permission to leave the club and move to Reggina.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hellasverona.it/news.php?id=5422 |publisher=Hellas Verona FC |title=Hellas Verona Football Club smentisce di essere alla ricerca di un nuovo allenatore |access-date=2007-06-27 |date=2007-06-27 |language=it |archive-date=2007-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928005322/http://www.hellasverona.it/news.php?id=5422 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun27r.html |publisher=Football Italia |title=Reggina coach poached! |access-date=2007-06-27 |date=2007-06-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701175034/http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun27r.html |archive-date=2007-07-01 |url-status=live }}</ref> On July 1, Reggina finally announced on their website to have appointed Ficcadenti as coach, after he successfully rescinded his contract with Verona.<ref name="ficcadenti_reggina"/> Ficcadenti was however sacked on November 1, following a 3–1 home loss to last-placed [[A.S. Livorno Calcio|Livorno]] and no wins in the first ten league days,<ref name="ficcadenti_sacked" /> and veteran coach [[Renzo Ulivieri]] was appointed to replace him.<ref name="ulivieri_reggina" /> However, on March 3, 2008 the club management decided to dismiss Ulivieri from his post following a 0–0 home draw to Palermo, as Reggina was filling the 19th place with 22 points, and replaced him with team scout and former youth team coach [[Nevio Orlandi]].<ref name="ulivieri_sacked" />
*'''Sampdoria''': on May 31, 2007 [[Walter Mazzarri]] was named new Samp boss.<ref name="mazzarri_samp"/>
*'''Siena''': on June 12, 2007 [[Andrea Mandorlini]] was confirmed new head coach following separation by mutual consent between the club and its boss [[Mario Beretta]].<ref name="mandorlini_siena"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Beretta ends Siena spell |url=http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun7n.html |publisher=Football Italia |date=2007-06-07 |access-date=2007-06-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070610230706/http://www.channel4.com/sport/football_italia/jun7n.html |archive-date=2007-06-10 |url-status=live }}</ref> However Mandorlini was sacked on November 12, after a 2–3 home loss to [[A.S. Livorno Calcio|Livorno]] which left the team in last place, and Beretta accepted to return at Siena.<ref name="mandorlini_sacked" />
*'''Torino''': on June 6, 2007 former [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] boss [[Walter Novellino]] was announced head coach for the new season, replacing [[Gianni De Biasi]].<ref name="novellino_toro"/> On April 16, 2008, following a string of disappointing results that left the ''granata'' only four points ahead the relegation zone, leading to heavy criticisms from the supporting fanbase, Torino president [[Urbano Cairo]] chose to sack Novellino and reappoint De Biasi, a fan favourite, as head coach.<ref name="novellino_sacked" />
*'''Udinese''': on June 5, 2007 former [[Calcio Catania|Catania]] boss [[Pasquale Marino]] was officially unveiled as new head coach.<ref name="marino_udinese"/>
